主要内容: Investors are showing strong interest in biotech companies working on innovative cancer treatments, particularly those developing CAR-T cell therapy. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration recently approved Novartis' Kymriah as the first drug using this new form of immunotherapy. Analysts highlight the potential for growth and acquisition as key reasons for their confidence in these stocks. Shares of companies like bluebird bio, Juno Therapeutics, and Nektar Therapeutics saw significant gains, with bluebird bio rising over 10 percent and Nektar Therapeutics nearly 8 percent. The iShares Nasdaq Biotechnology ETF (IBB) also reached its highest level since January 2016. The biotech sector is seen as a major driver of innovation in cancer treatment, with the potential to transform traditional methods of therapy. The overall cancer death rate in the U.S. has fallen by 13 percent from 2004 to 2013, indicating improving treatment outcomes. Investors are showing significant interest in pharmaceutical companies that are developing immunotherapy treatments for cancer. Merck and Bristol-Myers Squibb have already approved immunotherapy drugs, while Gilead Sciences is set to acquire Kite Pharma for $11.9 billion, which is expected to gain FDA approval for its CAR-T drug for lymphoma by November 29. Analysts note that cancer drugs are not subject to increased political pressure to lower prices, as seen with Novartis' Kymriah, which costs $475,000 for a one-time treatment. Michael Rich of Eagle Asset Management highlights that the high cost of these drugs makes it difficult for payers to push back on pricing. Additionally, pharmaceutical companies are looking to acquire smaller biotechnology firms due to the financial strain from generic drug competition. UBS reports that pharmaceutical companies hold over 15% of unrepatriated profits, with S&P 500 health-care companies holding $541 billion in overseas profits in 2016. While immunotherapy is still in early development, investors are advised to take a higher risk-return approach in this sector.
